result.title: Are We Rewarding the Wrong Module? Module-Specific Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) based on Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has been widely adopted to enhance the multimodal reasoning of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, existing methods share a common limitation of Module-Level Credit Entanglement, in which the vision encoder, projector, and LLM modules are jointly optimized using the same advantage signals even when perceptual correctness and final-answer correctness differ. To address this limitation, we propose Module-Specific Policy Optimization (MSPO), a framework that separates perceptual and outcome-based learning signals across model modules. Specifically, MSPO uses responses to perception checklists comprising auxiliary questions about visual information to derive an advantage for training the vision encoder. From these responses, MSPO computes the Confidence-aware Perception Reward (CaPR), using a perception sign obtained by thresholding checklist accuracy to determine reward direction and posterior confidence from a Beta distribution over latent perception accuracy to scale reward magnitude. We then derive the vision advantage through group-relative normalization of CaPR and scale it using main-task success rates. This advantage guides updates to the vision encoder, while the projector and LLM retain outcome-based GRPO updates. Extensive experiments on seven mathematical and general reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that MSPO outperforms existing RL-tuned models on average at both the 3B and 7B scales.

AI.brief_summary: 针对多模态 RLVR 中视觉编码器、projector 与 LLM 共用同一 advantage 的「模块级信用纠缠」问题，提出 MSPO：用感知清单问答构造置信度感知的感知奖励（阈值定方向、Beta 后验置信度定幅度），并结合主任务成功率缩放得到视觉编码器专属 advantage，其余模块仍用结果型 GRPO。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应「贡献分配与监督」主线，可供核查分离感知与结果信号能否缓解视觉旁路、感知奖励是否真让答案使用视觉证据，以及清单与额外前向的成本收益。
